_comment: Shape of ONE company's engagement scope as stored by Jade (JDE_COMPANY_SCOPE_DIR/<company_id>.json) -- the record the execution gate (mcp_server/jde_mcp_server/scope.py) enforces for that company's stories. Normally an Admin edits it under Admin > ERP / JDE Landscape, which stamps revision, updated_by and spike approvals server-side; hand-editing is only for running the MCP tools outside Jade. Filled in from a signed-off Configuration / Development Guidelines document (Appendix D.2 / E.2) -- never by an agent. A section left out authorises nothing; a missing or unrecognised approval_policy blocks approval and execution.
customer_id: <company id, e.g. bwm -- must match the file name>

environment._comment: DEV isolation must be demonstrated, not assumed from the name (Section 1). Execution is refused until isolation_confirmed is true, and Jade records who confirmed it and when.
environment.dev_environment_id: <e.g. JDV920 -- the exact JDE environment name>
environment.ais_data_source_name: <the data source this environment actually resolves to via OCM>
environment.isolation_evidence: <how OCM mappings were checked to confirm writes here cannot reach another environment's business data>

_comment_approval_policy: Enforced. Which company roles may approve an exact change (admin, product_manager, domain_owner) and how many hours an approval stays valid (1-168). Checked at approval and again immediately before execution. The gate refuses any field inside approval_policy it does not know, so keep comments out of it.

approved_versions.notes: Example only -- default document type on a named sales order version.

spike_experiments._comment: A capability at Needs spike runs ONLY inside a dated, explicitly approved DEV test window: this exact capability revision, target and environment, before expires_at (ISO-8601 with timezone). Missing, unreadable or past expiry allows nothing.
spike_experiments.capability_revision: <must equal capability_catalog.json's current revision for this capability>
spike_experiments.note: <what this experiment is meant to prove>

functional_agent._comment_reference_only: never_touch_categories and approvers are recorded for people and are NOT read by the gate; approval authority comes from approval_policy plus company roles.

technical_agent._comment_authorized_object_types: Subset of the four Web-OMW-native types from Section 7.6 this engagement actually wants: ExternalFormApplication, DataStructure, Workflow, BusinessView. Empty until the feasibility spike (Section 10.2) and customer sign-off both say yes.
technical_agent.reserved_product_code: <one value from 55-59, agreed with the customer>

_proposed_not_enforced._comment: PROPOSED design (Functional Agent design update, Section 5.1). Nothing below is read by the execution gate today and Jade does not store it; it is kept here so the intended shape is not lost.

protected_scope._comment: Additional safeguards beyond the universal XJDE/ZJDE and 55-59 rules in scope.py, and beyond each capability's own protected_targets in capability_catalog.json -- engagement-specific things that must never be touched regardless of any other approval.
prohibited_interfaces: <e.g. direct database access, spec table writes>
prohibited_record_types: <e.g. specific master data tables this engagement has flagged as off-limits>

mechanisms._comment: Explicit allowlist (Section 1: 'Direct database/specification writes are disabled in the normal agent toolset... failure of a supported route never authorises this fallback').

test_scope._comment: A test/verification action (a report submission, order creation, etc.) is itself an action requiring its own permitted scope -- configuration approval does not implicitly permit posting, payments, outbound integrations, or unrestricted batch execution (Section 5.3).
approved_test_fixtures: <e.g. specific DEV test customer/order records safe to use>
permitted_test_actions: run_orchestration against the named acceptance test
